title: Meera's Product Price Comparator
description:
Meera manages a small shop and wants to display her products sorted by price in descending order so the most expensive items appear at the top of her catalogue. She uses Java's Comparator interface to define a custom ordering that is separate from the product's natural order. Each product has a name and a price.

The program reads N products, sorts them by price in descending order using a Comparator, and prints the sorted list. A class PriceComparator implements Comparator« Product> and overrides the compare() method to return the difference of the second product's price minus the first product's price (this makes higher prices come first). The sortProducts() function uses a selection sort, passing the comparator to all comparisons via comparator.compare(). The main function reads the inputs, creates a PriceComparator, calls sortProducts(), and prints each product's name and price.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer N representing the number of products.
The second line contains N space-separated strings representing product names.
The third line contains N space-separated integers representing prices in the same order.
outputFormat: Print N lines. Each line consists of a product name followed by a space and its price, sorted in descending order of price.
constraints: Product names are single words with no spaces
explanation: Complete verified reference solution for Meera's Product Price Comparator. Solves problem constraints and handles all standard I/O format requirements.

title: Karan's Shopping Cart Vector
description:
Karan is building a basic shopping cart system. He uses a Vector to store the item prices added to a customer's cart. After all items are added, the system displays the total number of items, lists all item prices, and calculates the total cost.

The program uses two user-defined functions. The first function, addltems(), accepts the Vector and an array of prices, and adds each price to the Vector using the add() method. The second function, displayCart(), accepts the Vector and prints the size using size(), then iterates through it using an index-based loop with get() to print each price, and finally prints the total cost. The main function reads the input, calls both functions in order.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer N representing the number of items in the cart.
The second line contains N space-separated integers representing the price of each item.
outputFormat:
Print 'Items: <count>' on the first line.
Print each item price on a separate line.
Print 'Total: <sum>' on the final line.
explanation: Complete verified reference solution for Karan's Shopping Cart Vector. Solves problem constraints and handles all standard I/O format requirements.

title: Divya's Student Rank List Comparable
description:
Divya is a class teacher who needs to print the rank list of her students sorted by their marks in ascending order. She decides to use Java's Comparable interface to define the natural ordering for a Student class so that students can be sorted directly using any sort routine. Each student has a name and a marks value.

The program reads N students, sorts them by marks in ascending order using the natural ordering defined through Comparable, and prints the sorted list. The Student class implements Comparable« Student> and overrides the compareTo() method to compare students by their marks. The sortStudents() function uses a simple selection sort — for each position i it finds the student with the smallest marks among positions i to N-1 and swaps them into position i, using compareTo() for all comparisons. The main function reads the input, calls sortStudents(), and prints each student's name and marks.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer N representing the number of students.
The second line contains N space-separated strings representing the names of the students.
The third line contains N space-separated integers representing student marks in the same order.
outputFormat: Print N lines. Each line contains a student's name and marks, sorted in ascending order of marks.
constraints: Names are single words with no spaces
explanation: Complete verified reference solution for Divya's Student Rank List Comparable. Solves problem constraints and handles all standard I/O format requirements.

title: Sunita's Roll Number Attendance Iterator
description:
Sunita is a college coordinator who maintains an attendance list of student roll numbers. She stores the roll numbers in a Vector and uses an Iterator to traverse the list, printing each roll number and counting how many students are present. The program uses two user-defined functions.

The first function, loadRolls(), accepts the Vector and an array of roll numbers, and adds each roll number using the Vector's add() method. The second function, traverseAndCount(), accepts the Vector, obtains an Iterator using iterator(), and uses hasNext() and next() in a while loop to print each roll number and count the total. It then prints the count. The main function reads the input and calls both functions.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer N representing the number of students present.
The second line contains N space-separated integers representing roll numbers.
outputFormat:
Print each roll number on a separate line using an Iterator.
On the final line, print 'Count: <total>'.
explanation: Complete verified reference solution for Sunita's Roll Number Attendance Iterator. Solves problem constraints and handles all standard I/O format requirements.

title: Anita's Employee Multi-Level Comparable
description:
Anita is an HR manager who needs to generate a payroll report where employees are listed sorted by salary in ascending order. When two employees have the same salary, they must be listed in alphabetical order of their names. She uses Java's Comparable interface to encode this two-level ordering directly into the Employee class.

The Employee class implements Comparable« Employee> and overrides compareTo(): it first compares salaries, and if they are equal, it compares names using String.compareTo() to break the tie alphabetically. The sortEmployees() function uses selection sort with compareTo() for all comparisons. The main function reads N employees, calls sortEmployees(), and prints each employee's name and salary.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer N representing the number of employees.
The second line contains N space-separated strings representing employee names.
The third line contains N space-separated integers representing employee salaries in the same order.
outputFormat: Print N lines. Each line consists of an employee name and salary, sorted primarily by salary (ascending) and secondarily by name (alphabetically).
constraints: Names are single words with no spaces
explanation: Complete verified reference solution for Anita's Employee Multi-Level Comparable. Solves problem constraints and handles all standard I/O format requirements.

title: Vikram's Score Threshold Vector Filtering
description:
Vikram is a game developer who maintains player scores in a Vector. After each round, he wants to filter out all scores that fall below a given threshold, keeping only the qualifying scores. He uses an Iterator to traverse the Vector and the Iterator's remove() method to safely delete elements during traversal without causing errors. The program uses two user-defined functions.

The first function, loadScores(), adds all scores to the Vector using add(). The second function, filterAndDisplay(), accepts the Vector and a threshold. It obtains an Iterator using iterator() and uses hasNext() and next() in a while loop — if the current element is strictly less than the threshold, it calls it.remove() to remove it. After the loop, it prints the remaining elements using a second iterator and prints the remaining count. The main function reads all inputs and calls both functions.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer N representing the number of scores.
The second line contains N space-separated integers representing scores.
The third line contains an integer representing the threshold value.
outputFormat:
Print each filtered score greater than or equal to the threshold on a separate line.
On the final line, print 'Remaining: <count>'.
explanation: Complete verified reference solution for Vikram's Score Threshold Vector Filtering. Solves problem constraints and handles all standard I/O format requirements.

title: Deepa's StepRange Iterable & StepIterator
description:
Deepa is a maths teacher who wants to generate number sequences with a fixed step value for her classroom exercises. Given a start value, an end value, and a step size, she needs to produce all numbers from start to end (inclusive) that are reachable by adding the step repeatedly. = 2 produces: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9. A class StepRange implements Iterable« Integer> and holds the start, end, and step values.

It overrides the iterator() method and returns an inner class Steplterator that implements Iterator« Integer>. The inner class maintains a current variable initialised to start. hasNext() returns true while current is less than or equal to end. next() returns the current value and advances current by step. The main function creates a StepRange object, uses it in a for-each loop to print each value and count them, then prints the count.
inputFormat: The first line of input consists of three space-separated integers representing start, end, and step values of the range.
outputFormat:
Print each value in the step range on a separate line.
On the final line, print 'Total elements: <count>'.
explanation: Complete verified reference solution for Deepa's StepRange Iterable & StepIterator. Solves problem constraints and handles all standard I/O format requirements.

title: Rahul's Word Length & Alphabetical Comparator
description:
Rahul is building a word processing utility. He needs to sort a list of words first by their length in ascending order, and when two words have the same length, they should appear in alphabetical order. He uses a Comparator to define this custom two-level ordering without modifying the String class.

A class WordComparator implements Comparator <String> and overrides the compare() method: it first compares the lengths of the two strings, and if the lengths are equal, it uses String.compareTo() to compare them alphabetically. The sortWords() function uses selection sort with comparator.compare() for all comparisons. The main function reads N words, calls sortWords(), and prints each word on a new line.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer N representing the number of words.
The second line contains N space-separated strings representing the words.
outputFormat: Print N lines. Each line consists of a word and its length, sorted primarily by word length (ascending) and secondarily alphabetically.
constraints: All words are lowercase with no spaces
explanation: Complete verified reference solution for Rahul's Word Length & Alphabetical Comparator. Solves problem constraints and handles all standard I/O format requirements.

title: Sita's Library Book Page Sorter
description:
Sita manages a library catalogue. She needs to sort books first by number of pages in ascending order. When two books have the same page count, they should appear in alphabetical order by title. She first sorts using Comparable for the primary key (pages) and uses a Comparator as the tiebreaker (alphabetical title order).

The Book class implements and overrides compareTo() to compare only by page count. A separate class BookComparator implements Comparator« Book> and overrides compare(): it first calls compareTo() on the two books, and if the result is zero (equal pages), it breaks the tie by comparing titles alphabetically using String.compareTo(). The sortBooks() function uses selection sort with BookComparator for all comparisons. The main function reads N books, sorts them, and prints each book's title and page count.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer N representing the number of books.
The second line contains N space-separated strings representing book titles.
The third line contains N space-separated integers representing page counts.
outputFormat: Print N lines. Each line consists of a book title and page count, sorted in ascending order of page count.
constraints: Book titles are single words with no spaces
explanation: Complete verified reference solution for Sita's Library Book Page Sorter. Solves problem constraints and handles all standard I/O format requirements.

title: Priya's Logistics Delivery Time Window
description:
Priya is a logistics coordinator who tracks delivery time values (in minutes) stored in a Vector. Her manager asks her how many deliveries were completed within a given time window — that is, how many values fall between a lower bound and an upper bound, both inclusive. The DeliveryBatch class implements Iterable« Integer> and wraps a Vector internally. It overrides iterator() to return the Vector's own iterator, making the batch directly usable in a for-each loop.

The program uses two user-defined functions. The first function, loadDeliveries(), adds all values to the internal Vector. The second function, countlnRange(), accepts the DeliveryBatch object and the bounds low and high, iterates over it using a for-each loop, counts every element where low <= element high, and returns the count. The main function reads all inputs, calls both functions, and prints the result.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer N representing the number of deliveries.
The second line contains N space-separated integers representing delivery times in minutes.
The third line contains two space-separated integers representing low and high time thresholds.
outputFormat:
Print each delivery time falling strictly within [low, high] on a separate line.
On the final line, print 'In range: <count>'.
explanation: Complete verified reference solution for Priya's Logistics Delivery Time Window. Solves problem constraints and handles all standard I/O format requirements.

title: Rajan's Sensor Reading Vector Extremes
description:
Rajan is a data analyst who stores a batch of sensor readings in a Vector. He needs to find the maximum and minimum values in the batch. He uses an Iterator to traverse the entire Vector in a single pass, tracking the largest and smallest values seen so far. The program uses two user-defined functions.

The first function, loadData(), adds all readings to the Vector using add(). The second function, findMaxMin(), accepts the Vector, obtains an Iterator using iterator(), and uses hasNext() and next() to traverse all elements in one pass while maintaining max and min variables initialised to the first element. After the traversal it prints the maximum and minimum. The main function reads the inputs and calls both functions.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer N representing the number of sensor readings.
The second line contains N space-separated integers representing sensor readings.
outputFormat:
Print the maximum reading in the format 'Max: <val>'.
Print the minimum reading in the format 'Min: <val>'.
Print the average reading in the format 'Average: <val>'.
explanation: Complete verified reference solution for Rajan's Sensor Reading Vector Extremes. Solves problem constraints and handles all standard I/O format requirements.

title: Arjun's Player Score Threshold Filter
description:
Arjun is a game server developer who stores player scores in a Vector. After each game session, he needs to extract the top K scores in descending order to display on the leaderboard. He sorts the Vector using Comparable (by descending score order) and then uses an Iterator to extract the first K elements. The Score class implements and overrides compareTo() to sort in descending order (higher scores come first).

The program uses three user-defined functions. The first function, loadScores(), adds all Score objects to the Vector. The second function, sortVector(), applies a selection sort on the Vector using compareTo() via get() and set(). The third function, printTopK(), uses an Iterator to traverse the sorted Vector and prints exactly the first K score values, then stops. The main function reads all inputs and calls all three functions in order.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer N representing the number of players.
The second line contains N space-separated strings representing player names.
The third line contains N space-separated integers representing scores.
The fourth line contains an integer representing the qualifying threshold score.
outputFormat:
Print the qualifying players' names and scores (score >= threshold) in original order.
On the final line, print 'Qualified: <count>'.
constraints: Player names are single words with no spaces
explanation: Complete verified reference solution for Arjun's Player Score Threshold Filter. Solves problem constraints and handles all standard I/O format requirements.

title: Office Inventory Deposit & Daily Cost Tracker

a store manager, needs a program to manage inventory items. Define a class ItemType with private attributes for name, deposit, and cost per day.

title: Toll Booth Vehicle Registry using HashSet
description:
A city traffic management system needs to track vehicles entering a toll booth. Each vehicle is uniquely identified by its registration number.

The system should allow adding vehicles to a record, ensuring that no duplicate registration numbers exist. The vehicles should be stored in a HashSet, which does not guarantee any specific order. Your task is to implement a program using a HashSet that allows adding vehicle details and displaying the records.
inputFormat:
The first line of input contains an integer N representing the number of vehicles.
The next N lines contain details of each vehicle in the format:
"RegNumber OwnerName VehicleType"
- RegNumber (String): Unique alphanumeric registration number
- OwnerName (String): Name of the vehicle owner
- VehicleType (String): Car, Bike, or Truck
If a vehicle with the same registration number is already present, ignore the duplicate entry.
outputFormat: Print the unique vehicle records in the order they are inserted, one per line.
constraints: VehicleType is always either Car, Bike, or Truck
Duplicate registration numbers must be ignored

5
KA01AB1234 John Car
MH02CD5678 Alice Bike
DL03EF9012 Bob Truck
TN04GH3456 Mike Car
KA01AB1234 John Car

KA01AB1234 John Car
MH02CD5678 Alice Bike
DL03EF9012 Bob Truck
TN04GH3456 Mike Car

testCases.input:
5
KA01AB1234 John Car
MH02CD5678 Alice Bike
DL03EF9012 Bob Truck
TN04GH3456 Mike Car
KA01AB1234 John Car

KA01AB1234 John Car
MH02CD5678 Alice Bike
DL03EF9012 Bob Truck
TN04GH3456 Mike Car

testCases.input:
3
KA01A1000 Alex Car
KA01A1000 Alex Car
DL02B2000 Ben Bike
testCases.expectedOutput:
KA01A1000 Alex Car
DL02B2000 Ben Bike

explanation: Complete verified reference solution for Toll Booth Vehicle Registry using HashSet. Solves problem constraints and handles all standard I/O format requirements.

title: Arjun's Prime Number Combinations

title: Ananya's Coding Competition Leaderboard
description:
Ananya is organizing a coding competition at her college. After the evaluation round, she receives a list of participants along with their scores and submission times. • If both score and submission time are the same, sort them in lexicographical order of name. title: Restaurant Waitlist Queue Management System
